# `regex` — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 1 *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — Go regexp go1.26 (surveyed 2026-10-07, closed 2026-10-07)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-07 · mutation 2026-10-07

**Downstream consumer:** yes

**Go `regexp` API, one by one** (closed 2026-10-07; every row answered against Go by the oracle):
`Compile` → `Regex.compile`; `CompilePOSIX` → `compilePosix` / `Options{ .syntax = .posix }`;
`MustCompile` → `comptimeCompile` (a bad pattern is a compile error); `Match`/`MatchString` →
`matches`, `Regex.isMatch`; `MatchReader` → `isMatchReader`; `Find*Index`, `Find*SubmatchIndex` →
`Matcher.find` / `captures` (spans — the text is `Span.slice`); `FindAll*` → `Matcher.iterator`
(`next`, `nextCaptures`), a limit is the caller's loop; `FindReader*Index` → `findReader` /
`capturesReader`; `Expand*` → `Regex.expand`; `ReplaceAll*`, `ReplaceAllLiteral*`,
`ReplaceAll*Func` → `Matcher.replaceAll` / `replaceAllLiteral` / `replaceAllFunc` (to a
`std.Io.Writer`) and allocating `Regex.replaceAll` / `replaceAllLiteral`; `Split` →
`Matcher.split` / `Regex.split`; `QuoteMeta` → `quoteMeta`; `LiteralPrefix` → `literalPrefix`
(LITERAL_PREFIX below); `Longest` → `Regex.longest`; `NumSubexp` / `SubexpNames` / `SubexpIndex`
→ `groupCount` / `names` / `groupIndex`; `String` → `Regex.source`. Byte-slice and string twins
are one function here; `MarshalText`/`UnmarshalText` are Go's encoding interfaces (`source` and
`compile` are the same pair). Syntax: all of `regexp/syntax`'s Perl grammar incl. `\p{…}` with
Go 1.25's loose names and `Any`/`ASCII`/`Assigned`, and its POSIX grammar.

**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig engine that is linear-time AND allocation-free in the match
path AND comptime-compilable AND has captures; a `Regex` immutable and shareable, scratch held by
the caller (`Matcher`), so captures never die at the next search; typed compile-time limits
instead of a runtime blow-up; anchored on the reference by a differential oracle (none of the Zig
libraries documents one); a compile cheap enough to run per call (stack scratch, ~0.2–0.5 µs for
a short pattern); every documented Go script name works (Go 1.26 refuses 46); a reader front end
in constant memory without an allocator. **Speed against Go 1.26** (2026-10-07, x86-64,
ReleaseFast vs `go build`, 24 shared workloads, same match counts on all; scratch bench, numbers
are ours/Go time): no-match scans of 1 MiB — literal 0.23, `[XYZ]ABC…` 0.10, twelve-way
alternation 0.28, `(?i)` 0.08; find-all over bxp rows 0.21–0.89; over 1 MiB of Czech/Greek/
Cyrillic text (`\p{L}+`, `\b\w+\b`, `(?i)žluť\w*`, …) 0.15–0.79; short-string submatches
0.43–0.95; compile + match per call 0.19–0.29. **Where we are behind:** speed in three places —
`[ -~]*ABC…$` over 1 MiB 1.28× (the Pike VM re-walks its start closure every byte, as Go's NFA
does), `INV-([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4})` find-all over 85 KiB 1.27× (too long for the backtracker's bit
budget, so the Pike VM with per-thread captures), an anchored find-all 101 vs 65 ns; no DFA (Go
has none either; RE2 and Rust do). Unicode tables are 15.0 (Go 1.26's); quangdn42/regex.zig
carries 17.0. CAPACITY: 1024 instructions and nesting 250, where Go allocates further.
**Head-to-head with quangdn42/regex.zig** (bxp's engine, commit `a22a2e68`, both through their
public APIs, 2026-10-07, x86-64 ReleaseFast, same answers on every case): per row with the
pattern compiled per call (bxp's REGEX_MATCH / REGEX_EXTRACT, nine template patterns × eight memo
rows) ours/quangd = 0.24 (0.14–0.43 per case); precompiled find-all over 83 KiB = 0.32 overall,
behind only on `#([0-9]+)` (1.80) — measured before the backtracker and the literal prefilter,
which made our find-all 1.3–4.5× faster again.

## What this module is, and what it is not

A matcher for RE2's language with RE2's guarantee: time linear in pattern × input. It is not a
PCRE: backreferences, lookaround, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers and recursion are refused
by design (`error.InvalidEscape` / `error.InvalidPerlOp`), because each of them needs
backtracking. It has no DFA: dense scans of long texts run at Go's speed, not RE2's.

## Design & invariants

- **One parse → AST → Thompson program.** `syntax.Builder` holds every table at fixed capacity
  (`max_insts` 1024, 4096 ranges, 2048 AST nodes, 64 groups); the same code runs at run time
  (builder on the heap, tables copied out) and at comptime (`comptimeCompile`). A pattern past a
  capacity is an error, never a truncated program.
- **Classes are sorted, merged code-point ranges**, matched by binary search. A class with the
  same ranges as an earlier one in the pattern points at those (`\p{L}` is ~700 ranges). `(?i)` folds each
  class member *before* its own negation and the class's `^` after that (Go's order:
  `(?i)\W` excludes U+017F and U+212A, which fold into `\w`).
- **Case folding is Unicode's simple folding as orbits** (`casefold.zig`, generated from Go's
  `unicode.SimpleFold`): 366 runs, each mapping a code point to its orbit successor by a constant
  delta or as alternating upper/lower pairs. A class folds run by run — the successors of a range
  are ranges — taken `max_orbit - 1` (3) times, so even `(?i)[\x{0}-\x{10FFFF}]` costs a few
  hundred ranges and compiles at comptime; a literal walks its orbit directly.
- **Unicode classes** (`unicode_tables.zig`, generated from Go's `unicode`): the 30 two-letter
  categories and 163 scripts are stored as LEB128-varint ranges (11 KB); every other name
  (`L`, `LC`, `Letter`, …) is a list of those, checked by the generator against Go's table for
  every code point. A name is looked up in its loose form (ASCII case, spaces, `_`, `-` dropped);
  `Any`, `ASCII` and `Assigned` (the complement of `Cn`) are computed. Folded and negated in
  Go's order, like a Perl class.
- **POSIX syntax** (`Syntax.posix`, Go's `CompilePOSIX`): the Perl escapes, `\p`, `\Q`, the
  assertions `\b \A \z` and every `(?…)` are refused; `^`/`$` are line anchors; a negated class
  gets `\n` added before negation; a repetition may repeat a repetition, so `a*?` is `(a*)?`; a
  `-` is a class member only first or last. Leftmost-longest by default.
- **Two builders.** `Regex.compile` first tries `syntax.BuilderOf(small_capacity)` on the stack (~9 KiB)
  and falls back to the full `Builder` from the allocator only on `error.PatternTooLarge`; the
  same parse runs in both, so the verdict is the full builder's. Never `b.* = .{}` on a builder or
  a VM state set: a default-initialised table is written whole (measured: 85 % of `isMatch` and
  most of a short compile before 2026-10-07's fix).
- **Prefilter** (`analyze`, once per program): `anchored` when every path from the start passes
  `\A` before consuming or matching; `lit` = up to 16 bytes of the literal prefix (below), found
  by a 32-byte first-and-last-byte vector scan when it has two bytes or more — never one holding
  U+FFFD, which an invalid byte also matches; `first` = the UTF-8 lead bytes of every class reachable
  without consuming (none when the match can be empty, a `.` is reachable, or a class holds U+FFFD
  — an invalid byte reads as U+FFFD and could start mid-sequence). Consulted only while no thread
  is alive, so it changes where the search looks, never which match it finds; a skip lands on an
  ASCII or lead byte, which always begins a code point the VM would decode.
- **`x*` over an `x` that can match empty compiles as `(x+)?`**, so one empty pass through `x`
  counts and its groups take part — Go's answer for `(a*)*` on `""` (group 1 = `[0,0]`).
- **The VM.** Thread lists in priority order; a match cuts the lower-priority threads of its step
  (leftmost-first). Leftmost-longest cuts nothing and drops threads that started after the
  match; the match state holds one thread per step, so the first to reach it at the longest end
  is the leftmost-first among equals (Go's documented choice). Empty transitions are followed with an explicit stack (no recursion), each
  state once per step, assertions judged from the code points on either side. An unanchored search
  starts a new thread at every position until a match is found. `isMatch`/`fullMatch` keep state
  sets on the stack (no captures); `Matcher` keeps per-thread capture slots in scratch made once.
- **The backtracker** (leftmost-first only): while (positions × instructions) ≤ 256 Kbit (Go's
  bound), `Matcher` searches depth-first with one visited bit per (position, instruction), so
  every state is explored once — linear, like the VM — and carries one set of captures instead
  of a copy per thread (short-string submatches 4–11× faster than the VM). The bits are kept
  across start positions (a state that failed fails from any start) and only the used prefix is
  cleared afterwards; past 16 Ki pending jobs, or on OOM, the search goes to the Pike VM. The
  robustness driver and the fuzz harness compare the two engines, groups included.
- **Reader front end.** Both VMs read through a text adapter; for a `std.Io.Reader` it is a
  window of two code points decoded exactly as a slice (U+FFFD one byte wide, the rest of a bad
  sequence left unread), so the reader is never read more than three code points past a match.
  No prefilter skipping (the bytes would have to be read anyway). A reader error before the
  answer is settled is `error.ReadFailed`; after it, the answer stands.
- **On top of a search** (`replace.zig`): `expand` reads Go's template grammar (names of Unicode
  letters, digits and `_`, greedy; a group number is ASCII digits without a leading zero; a
  repeated name means the first such group that took part); `SplitIterator` keeps Go's edges (an
  empty match at 0 splits nothing off, nothing after a match at the very end, an empty input is
  one empty piece unless the pattern is empty); `literalPrefix` follows every path from the start
  and grows while all live paths consume the same code point.
- **Text.** UTF-8 per code point; an invalid sequence is U+FFFD one byte wide (Go's reading);
  the code point before a search's start counts for `^`, `\b`.

## Threat model

Patterns and input may both be hostile. Time is O(pattern × input) by construction, in both
engines; memory is bounded by the compile-time capacities and the backtracker's fixed budget
(≤ 32 KiB of bits, ≤ 16 Ki jobs) — no allocation grows with the input. Compile work is
bounded too: nested counted repetitions multiply to at most 1000 (Go's rule — an empty body emits
nothing, so the instruction capacity alone would not stop `((a{0}){1000}){1000}…`). The parser and
compiler recurse once per nesting level, bounded by `max_depth` (250) — a deeply nested pattern
is refused, not a stack overflow; the deepest accepted one compiles on a 512 KiB thread stack in a
Debug build (tested).

## Verification

`src/go_oracle_test.zig` replays Go `regexp` (see Anchoring); `src/root.zig` holds unit tests per
feature and a deterministic robustness driver (20,000 random patterns × 4 inputs, invalid UTF-8
included: compile-or-refuse, the entry points agree, the prefilter only skips, the backtracker and
the Pike VM give the same groups at every start, no trap).

**Second round (2026-10-07, the parity work: `\p`, POSIX, leftmost-longest, the API on top,
the reader, the backtracker, the literal prefilter).** *Oracle:* every Perl-syntax case replayed
again after `Longest()` (279 cases differ from leftmost-first, all agree), two POSIX sets, every
Unicode class name, ReplaceAll with 31 templates / Literal / Func / Split / FindAllSubmatchIndex /
LiteralPrefix on 460 patterns, QuoteMeta of every ASCII byte, and every case once more through a
reader yielding one byte per read; planted bugs fail it (a reader that leaves continuation bytes:
1,541 cases; swapped backtracker branches: 8 tests). *Review* (independent, read-only, Go probed
for every claim): 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 3 LOW, 2 INFO. **HIGH (fixed)** — `\x{D800}` (Go compiles
it) hit `catch unreachable` in the literal-prefix walk on every compile, and was a compile error
under `comptimeCompile`; a surrogate is now written as U+FFFD, Go's `LiteralPrefix`. **MEDIUM
(fixed)** — `expand` with a repeated name took the first group by index; Go takes the first of
that name that took part. **LOW (fixed)** — a reader failing in the look-ahead after a settled
match became `error.ReadFailed`; the backtracker's job stack was unbounded (~12 MB worst case,
now 16 Ki then the Pike VM); a `std.Io.Reader` with a buffer under 4 bytes (not `fixed`) trips
std's own assert in `peek` — documented. INFO: the fuzz inputs never reached the 32-byte scan
(now repeated to 400 bytes now and then). *Mutation* (schemata, ReleaseSafe, whole suite): 42
mutants over the new code — loose names, `\p{^…}`, folding of `\p`, `Assigned`, `ASCII`, the
varint decoder, class sharing, every POSIX rule, longest's start cut and its POSIX default,
the backtracker's bookkeeping, restores, branch order and longest guard, the vector scan and its
tail, the reader's toss and window, Expand's `$$` / leading zero / `}` / Unicode names, Split's
edges and limit, QuoteMeta, literalPrefix's `\A`, ranges and completeness, the U+FFFD
exclusion: 37 killed, 2 survivors closed by tests (`\p{ASCII}` at 0x7f; `${a b}`), 3 equivalent
(the longest mode's equal-end check — dead, one match thread per step, removed; the backtracker's
anchored early exit — speed only; a redundant count in completeness). *Fuzz:* the harness also
compares the two engines, the reader with the slice, longest with first, and checks
`replaceAll("$0")` is the input, `replaceAllLiteral("")` removes exactly the matches, split
pieces miss the matches, every match begins with `literalPrefix`, `quoteMeta(input)` matches
the input; a share in POSIX syntax, an eighth of the inputs repeated to ~400 bytes: 200,000
runs clean (2,800/s, ReleaseSafe).

**First round (2026-10-07, the core engine).** *Mutation:* 34 mutants — lazy marker, `(?U)`,
repeat-size bounds, nested repetition, flag-group scope, `(?-i)`, octal backreference refusal,
`\s`, class negation, Kelvin fold, POSIX negation, `[a-]`, alternation patching, greedy/lazy
split order (star and counted), the empty-able star, per-member fold, Perl-class fold before
negation, punctuation escapes, unanchored restart, leftmost-first cut, `end_line`/`begin_line`,
`_` as a word character, `runeBefore`, empty-match adjacency and rune-width advance of the
iterator, range binary search, full-match end check, capture restore, split order in both VMs:
31 killed, 2 equivalent after 7 crafted oracle patterns were added; no code defect. *Review:* 1
HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 4 LOW, 5 INFO. **HIGH (fixed)** — nested counted repetitions of an empty body
emit no instructions, so no capacity stopped `(?:(?:(?:a{0}){1000}){1000}){1000}` (~10⁹ emit
calls); now Go's rule — the product of nested counted repetitions may not exceed 1000 — and
verdict. **MEDIUM (fixed)** — 1000 nested groups overflowed a 512 KiB thread stack in Debug;
`max_depth` is 250 and the compiler frames are small (tested on a 512 KiB thread). **LOW
(fixed):** `a(?i)*`, `\` before a control character, `\x{+41}`/`\x{4_1}`/`\x+1`/
`\x{000000041}`, `from` past the input. *Fuzz:* `src/fuzz_test.zig` (grammar-drawn patterns, a
share damaged byte-wise; the entry points agree, spans well-formed, a literal-only pattern
matches where `std.mem.indexOf` does), driver `REGEX_FUZZ`.

## Backlog / deferred

- **Speed past Go's: a lazy DFA with a caller-owned cache** *(survey 2026-10-07)* — RE2's and
  Rust's; would take the three cases where we trail Go (dense `[ -~]*…`, long-text find-all with
  captures) well past it. Not needed for parity. Fits §2 with caller-owned scratch.
- **Capacity past 1024 instructions / nesting 250** *(2026-10-07; kept as the listed CAPACITY
  divergence by the user's decision, may be revisited)* — Go compiles `a{1000}b{1000}`; here
  `error.PatternTooLarge`. Would need a heap program and heap VM scratch for large patterns while
  small ones stay allocation-free.
- **An ASCII bitmap per class, a one-pass engine** *(2026-10-07)* — smaller constant factors.
- **Fuzz: a POSIX grammar of its own** *(2026-10-07)* — the shared grammar reaches POSIX in ~1 %
  of runs (most random patterns use Perl syntax POSIX refuses).
- **Refresh the quangdn42/regex.zig head-to-head** *(2026-10-07)* — taken before the backtracker
  and the literal prefilter.
- **`RegexSet`** *(survey 2026-10-07)* — Rust's and RE2's, not Go's.
- **Unicode 17.0** — follows Go: regenerate the tables when Go's `unicode` moves.
- **Sibling modules that can now adopt it** *(2026-10-07)* — `validate` (`Pattern.matcher` takes a
  caller-supplied matcher today; a `regex` default), `jsonshape` (RFC 9535 `match()`/`search()`
  need I-Regexp, an RE2 subset), `tsdb` (regex label matchers), `probe` (`expect` regex). Each is
  that module's own backlog item; listed here so the dependency is visible.

## Status

`gap · any · util · reentrant` + deps: none — canonical source is `pub const meta` in src/root.zig.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it. A pattern is a portable text: one written for Go/RE2 must mean the same here.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — published vectors, goldens captured from a foreign implementation, or a test run against a live foreign peer.

**What the tests actually contain.** `tools/go_regexp_oracle` drives Go 1.26 `regexp` as a black
box over ~280 crafted syntax cases, every Unicode class name with the code points on its edges,
600 seeded random Perl patterns and two POSIX sets, and freezes the answers into
`src/go_vectors.zig`: compile verdict, group names, and per input `MatchString`, a full match,
`FindStringSubmatchIndex` and `FindAllStringIndex` — again after `Longest()` — plus, for 460
patterns, `ReplaceAllString` (31 templates), `ReplaceAllLiteralString`, `ReplaceAllStringFunc`,
`Split`, `FindAllStringSubmatchIndex` and `LiteralPrefix`, and `QuoteMeta` of every ASCII byte.
`tools/go_unicode` and `tools/go_casefold` derive the tables from Go's `unicode` and check them
for every code point. `src/go_oracle_test.zig` requires every answer, through a slice and through
a one-byte-per-read reader; the listed divergences are counted and pinned — GO_DEFECT (46: the
multi-word script names Go refuses), LITERAL_PREFIX (5: ours extends Go's), CAPACITY (5: past
1024 instructions or 250 levels). On the interop lane via `zig build interop-regex -- --check`.
Teeth: its first run found four defects (see tools/README.md); planted bugs fail it (see
Verification). Still self-graded: behaviour past the capacities (only the error is checked).
